environment.description: Application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB with AWS WAFv2 WebACL attached. The WebACL includes three rule groups evaluated in priority order: (1) AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet at priority 100 in COUNT mode for baseline telemetry, (2) a custom rule group 'corp-input-validation' at priority 200 that applies a regex pattern set matching UNION/SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE keywords with word-boundary anchors in URI query string components and blocks with 403, (3) AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet at priority 300 in BLOCK mode. Additionally, the ALB access logs feed into a Kinesis stream processed by a Lambda that triggers automated IP blocking via WAF IP sets when anomalous query patterns are detected within a 60-second window. The Fargate task uses a read-only root filesystem with an ephemeral tmpfs at /tmp only; the /var/data path is backed by an EFS access point configured with uid/gid enforcement and POSIX permissions 0444 on the database file, preventing any write operations including SQLite WAL/journal creation.

config.load_balancer: AWS ALB with WAFv2 WebACL 'prod-api-acl' attached
config.compute: ECS Fargate, read-only root filesystem, tmpfs at /tmp only
config.storage: EFS access point at /var/data, POSIX 0444 on app.db, no WAL/journal possible
config.network: ALB -> Fargate task in private subnet, no direct access
config.monitoring: ALB logs -> Kinesis -> Lambda auto-IP-block on anomaly detection
